The earliest sharks appeared roughly 450 million years ago, while the first true trees (like Archaeopteris) didn’t show up until around 385 million years ago. That means sharks were cruising the oceans for something like 60 million years before there was a single forest on land.

Your stomach grows a new lining every few days. Stomach acid is strong enough to start dissolving metal, so the cells lining your stomach are constantly being damaged. Your body handles this by replacing the surface layer every 3 to 5 days and covering it in a thick layer of protective mucus. If that turnover stopped, your stomach would slowly start digesting itself.
